headline: Local Momo Stall Owner Mistakenly Deported To Diplomatic Summit After Confusing 'Extra Chutney' Request With State Policy
body:
Birendra Sharma, a long-time proprietor of a popular street-side momo cart, found himself unexpectedly addressing a high-level bilateral trade delegation on Tuesday after he was accidentally ushered into the conference hall while attempting to deliver a delayed order of steamed chicken dumplings.

Following the recent policy shift emphasizing regional cooperation, security personnel reportedly confused Sharma’s energetic insistence that his customer 'take the sauce, it’s not an attack on your taste buds' for a profound geopolitical statement on cross-border relations. The stall owner was promptly given a microphone and allowed to speak for forty-five minutes before officials realized his 'strategic roadmap for regional integration' was actually a detailed plan to standardize the ratio of spicy garlic dip per plate.

'I just wanted the gentleman in the blue suit to stop saying my spice levels were aggressive,' said Sharma, while being escorted back to his cart by protocol officers. 'I told them the era of seeing my kitchen as a battleground is over, but they kept asking me about maritime trade routes. Eventually, I just agreed that the chutney is a bridge between nations, and they gave me a standing ovation.'
caption: When you accidentally become the face of foreign policy because you just really wanted to get rid of the extra spicy dip. #Diplomacy #MomoDiplomacy #InternationalRelations #StreetFood (satire)
igHook: Have you ever accidentally ended up in a meeting you weren't invited to?
